correctness.rationale: Gaussian normalization gives Dirichlet(1/2,...,1/2); inclusion-exclusion is exact. Marginal integrals (1) and (2) follow directly. At each threshold the scaled simplex beta integral yields coefficient B_{d,k} with no missing normalization; analytic lower-order terms and positive coefficients imply precisely the stated regularity. The upper endpoint follows by a separate complement-simplex argument, not extrapolation. The low-dimensional closed form and 69 numerical checks agree. Limits are all fixed d; no uniform-in-d claim.

No accessible text established a theorem that implies all requested k-onsets.

A Dirichlet density supplies starting integrals but not a printed claim of every positive onset coefficient or exact differentiability. The two inaccessible prior papers remain risks, not asserted NOT_COVERING from abstracts.

originality.rationale: The finite-dimensional spherical-coordinate Dirichlet density is classical and not claimed new. The candidate-specific contribution is the complete nonzero gamma coefficient at every sqrt(k) contact threshold, plus the resulting exact CDF differentiability hierarchy. Finch works with projection widths, Ciccariello with isotropic probes, Coleman with three incompletely specified random-probe measures, and Steinerberger with random high-dimensional chord statistics. The latter two full texts were unavailable, leaving residual risk; no inspected source implies the all-depth singularity classification. Targeted database and literature searches checked reciprocal maximum, all-dimensional Dirichlet equivalence, and spherical cube intersections without a covering result.
residual_risks: Exact prior random-probe sampling definitions in Coleman (1981) were unavailable; if one is a fixed-center probe the d=3 special CDF may already be known.
Steinerberger (2011) treats high-dimensional cube random chords; full text was unavailable and could include a stronger result; no claim of definitive worldwide priority.
General order-statistic literature for symmetric Dirichlet(1/2) maxima may implicitly or explicitly present the same endpoint coefficients under different language.

value.rationale: Natural Haar-direction central-chord distribution of the d-cube, essential for radial geometric tomography, admits a nontrivial sequence of d geometrically forced contact thresholds. Explicit nonzero coefficients classify all changes in regularity and describe the final vertex tail. The result is independent of support-width distributions and provides much more structure than a mean, a single onset, or a routine finite table. Its exact value is the all-depth geometry/regularity classification with full CDF integrals; no claim to new Dirichlet densities.
